items.actClause:
AN ACT authorizing the commissioner of transportation to conduct a
comprehensive study on designation of private roads on the University at
Buffalo North Campus for the purposes of autonomous vehicle technology testing
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6052

SPONSOR: KENNEDY
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act authorizing the commissioner of transportation
to conduct a comprehensive study on designation of private roads on the
University at Buffalo North Campus for the purposes of autonomous vehi-
cle technology testing

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To study the traffic flow of roads around the University at Buffalo
North Campus for the capability of autonomous vehicle technology test-
ing.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 sets forth the legislative intent

Section 2 defines "autonomous vehicle technology" for the purposes of
this act

Section 3 directs DOT to undertake a comprehensive study

Section 4 directs the DOT to issue a report within one year of this
act's effective date

Section 5 sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

With the rise of autonomous vehicle technology, the University at
Buffalo has been on the cutting edge of testing the capabilities of
various autonomous vehicles in development. However, AV vehicles tested
at the University at Buffalo are currently limited on which roadways
testing can occur to private roads and parking lots.

By having the New York State DOT study the traffic flows on roadways
around the University at Buffalo's North Campus, date and information
will be gathered on what additional roadways can be used for such test-
ing, giving the University at Buffalo additional options for testing
this emerging technology.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately

A.actClause:
AN ACT authorizing the commissioner of transportation to conduct a
comprehensive study on designation of private roads on the University at
Buffalo North Campus and public roads in the town of Amherst for the purposes
of autonomous vehicle technology testing
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6052A

SPONSOR: KENNEDY
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act authorizing the commissioner of transportation
to conduct a comprehensive study on designation of private roads on the
University at Buffalo North Campus and public roads in the town of
Amherst for the purposes of autonomous vehicle technology testing

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To study the traffic flow of roads around the University at Buffalo
North Campus for the capability of autonomous vehicle technology test-
ing.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 sets forth the legislative intent

Section 2 defines "autonomous vehicle technology" for the purposes of
this act

Section 3 directs DOT to undertake a comprehensive study as well as
establishes the scope of said study, including the creation of three
testing zones in the town of Amherst. Subsection two of section three
authorizes the Erie County Sheriff, University at Buffalo Campus Police
and Town of Amherst Police to supervise autonomous vehicle testing.
Subsection four of section three establishes that insurance requirements
for fleets during testing are in line with current requirements
prescribed in the vehicle and traffic law

Section 4 directs the DOT to issue a report to the governor and legisla-
ture of its findings, conclusions, and recommendations no later than six
months after the effective date of this act. Moreover, it directs DOT to
promulgate the necessary regulations relating to section three of this
act no later than ninety days after delivering its report

Section 5 sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

With the rise of autonomous vehicle technology, the University at
Buffalo has been on the cutting edge of testing the capabilities of
various autonomous vehicles in development. However, autonomous vehicles
tested at the University at Buffalo are currently limited on which road-
ways testing can occur on, to private roads and parking lots.  By having
the New York State DOT study the traffic flows on roadways around the
University at Buffalo's North Campus, date and information will be gath-
ered on what additional roadways can be used for such testing, giving
the University at Buffalo additional options for testing this emerging
technology.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately
